Customs Act 2023: This Act provides the legal authority under Section 25(1) for the government to grant specific tax exemptions on imported goods used for power generation.
Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty A: Section 126(1) of this Act empowers the government to grant exemptions from Value Added Tax for specified goods imported for power generation projects.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is consulted by the government to determine the conditions and extent of tax exemptions granted for specific imported goods used in the power sector.
Imported Goods: Coal classified under the specified H.S. Code is eligible for a Value Added Tax exemption on the portion exceeding five percent, provided it is imported for use in power generation plants.
H.S. Code: The specified H.S. Code for coal is subject to a partial Value Added Tax exemption when imported for power production purposes, subject to strictly defined documentation and certification requirements.
TABLE: The table identifies specific coal commodities by H.S. Code that qualify for Value Added Tax concessions when imported for power generation purposes.
Customs Clearance: To qualify for the tax exemption, importers must submit a certificate from the Power Division, a detailed packing list, and a formal undertaking to the Customs Commissioner at the time of clearing each coal consignment.

Statutory Regulatory Order: This order is considered to have come into effect on a specific date in June two thousand twenty-four and shall remain in force until a designated date in June two thousand twenty-six.

Power Generation Plant: A power generation plant, whether public or private, is defined as a project established under a contract with the Government of Bangladesh.
The plant must have commenced commercial operations to be eligible for specific certifications regarding their imports.
Coal Import: Imports of coal by an eligible power generation plant must be certified as directly related to electricity production.
Certified coal imports are strictly limited to use within the specific power generation facility for which they were imported.

Customs Act 2023: This Act serves as the legal framework for taking enforcement actions, including the recovery of duties and taxes, in instances where imported goods are utilized for purposes other than those officially declared.
Imported Goods: The importer must provide a formal undertaking stating that the imported coal is directly related to power generation and will be used exclusively at the designated power plant. If the goods are diverted for unauthorized purposes or locations, the importer is legally obligated to pay all applicable duties and taxes.
